thread:
sara: quick heads-up — I sketched a tiny change to quota routing for API keys. current behavior -> key maps to global quota unless it's a project-scoped key. proposal: prefer X-Redwood-Project header -> route to project quota; else if key has org claim route to org quota; else fallback to global. console should show "effective quota" and which bucket served the request. comments?

jules: +1 to showing effective bucket in console. question: how do we handle service-account tokens that assert both project and org? prefer project, right?

sara: yes prefer project. ordering: project header -> key.project claim -> key.org claim -> global. keeps routing deterministic.

kevin: need telemetry to prove it doesn't regress per-key QPS. propose adding a metric: `redwood.quota.route.v1{bucket}` with tags: bucket=project|org|global, key_id, project_id? maybe mask key_id for PII.

marta: agree on metric. also want an alert if >1% of requests switch buckets for same key within a minute — that usually signals header flakiness.

omar: small implementation nit: routing decision happens in the auth layer today, but quota enforcement happens downstream in quota service. we can shove the routing decision into the auth proxy and pass `X-Redwood-Quota-Bucket: project:proj-123` to quota service. lightweight change.

jules: sounds good. UX: on the console quotas page can we show the last 24h breakdown by bucket and a line graph of switches? path: /console/usage/{org}/keys/{key}/quota-route. simple table + sparkline is enough.

sara: agreed. include a tooltip: "Effective quota = bucket used for most requests in last 5m".

kevin: smoke test plan — canary on staging then 10% prod for 2h. test matrix: 
- create project-scoped key -> curl should route to project bucket
- create plain org key -> routes to org bucket
- no-claims key -> global bucket

Example curl for smoke test:
```bash
API_KEY=sk_test_project123
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" 
  -H "X-Redwood-Project: proj-123" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"prompt":"test"}' 
| jq .meta.quota_bucket
```
Expected: `project:proj-123`

marta: add a telemetry check: run 1000 requests for each key type and assert failure rate and that `redwood.quota.route.v1{bucket=...}` counts match what console shows.

omar: flag: `ff.quota_routing.v2` set to canary-by-org. rollout plan: orgs in canary list get the routing header from auth proxy.

jules: UX rollout note — console should gracefully backfill. if ff off, console shows legacy routing. migrate historical usage in telemetry pipeline for the new metric name.

sara: sgtm. I'll open a PR with the proxy change + test harness + dashboard panel JSON. planning to schedule the canary 10:30am PST tomorrow.

deploy-bot: deploy started: auth-proxy-3f9a (ff.quota_routing.v2=true for canary orgs) — build 2026.3.18-08:30

kevin: smoke test results from staging: project-key -> project (1000/1000), org-key -> org (995/1000, 5 header timeouts), global -> global (1000/1000). hitting the alert for switching was triggered by header timeouts — looks like transient network.

marta: ok re-run with retry/backoff in client for header timeouts. also patch console to mark 5 requests as "flappy" in UI.

sara: thanks — I'll hold prod rollout until we confirm retries reduce switch rate below 0.1%. will kick off another run in 30min. :thumbsup:
